page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with Geekbench and stress-ng single-core tests placing in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by the stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, reaching 76.43 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads, though the Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform at average levels, achieving 11.3 million operations per second.

Given the high memory density relative to compute resources, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require substantial memory capacity but do not demand high single-threaded CPU performance. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which aligns with its 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The ecs.se1.4xlarge is best suited for memory-intensive applications such as in-memory caching, medium-sized database hosting, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing tasks that benefit from its 128 GB RAM capacity.
